Troubleshoot

Source: vignettes/Troubleshoot.Rmd
Troubleshoot.Rmd

For problems with the Python setup, extra downloads or your own Python environment, see Installation and setup. For GPUs, see the GPU article.

Reporting a problem

birdnet_sitrep() shows which Python environment birdnetR uses:

birdnet_sitrep()
#> python_version: 3.12.14
#> python_executable: /home/user/.cache/uv/archive-v0/0MLD8yprGexELXHg/bin/python
#> birdnet_version: 1.5.0
#> runtimes: onnxruntime, ai_edge_litert
  • python_version, python_executable: the Python that birdnetR runs on.
  • birdnet_version: the version of the birdnet Python package.
  • runtimes: the installed inference runtimes (any of onnxruntime, ai_edge_litert (LiteRT), tensorflow and torch).

Please include this output when you report a bug.

After birdnetR has installed TensorFlow or PyTorch during a session (see Extra downloads), python_executable points to a different folder than before. That is expected: reticulate adds the new packages as an extra layer on top of the existing environment.

Long wait on the first load

The first load of a model can take several minutes without visible progress: birdnetR is downloading Python packages, and for TensorFlow or PyTorch that is 600 MB to several GB. See Download progress.

as.data.frame() is slow on large results

birdnet_predict() keeps its results in Python. as.data.frame() copies them into R, which takes time and memory when there are many detections, for example with many hours of audio, a low min_confidence or top_k = NULL.

If you don’t need the results in R right away, write them to a file instead. birdnet_write() writes CSV, Parquet or NumPy files straight from Python:

birdnet_write(predictions, "results.csv")

For tips on processing many files, see Process many files.

High memory or CPU use

birdnet_predict() and birdnet_encode() start several worker processes, and each loads its own copy of the model. On the CPU, birdnet starts one worker per physical core (fewer when memory is short) and keeps all cores busy. Full CPU load during a run is expected.

If memory runs out, or the computer becomes unresponsive, lower n_workers and batch_size:

predictions <- birdnet_predict(model, files, n_workers = 2L, batch_size = 1L)
  • n_workers is the number of model copies in memory. TensorFlow and PyTorch workers need more memory than ONNX Runtime ones.
  • batch_size is the number of segments each worker processes at once. Larger values need more memory.

Fewer workers mainly save memory: birdnet gives each worker more CPU threads, so the CPU stays busy. If a worker is killed because memory ran out, birdnet stops with an error that names the worker.

With device = "GPU", birdnetR starts one worker per GPU. A larger n_workers puts another copy of the model on the GPU for each extra worker; see Workers and batch size.

Parallel processing

Don’t run birdnetR inside parallel or future workers (for example with parallel::parLapply(), future.apply::future_lapply() or furrr). Each worker is a fresh R session without birdnetR’s Python setup, so birdnet does not work reliably there (see #56).

birdnet_predict() and birdnet_encode() already run in parallel. Pass all files in one call and set the number of parallel workers with n_workers:

predictions <- birdnet_predict(model, files, n_workers = 8L)

Harmless console messages

  • Decoding MP3 files (for example the bundled soundscape.mp3) can print libmpg123 errors such as part2_3_length ... too large. The results are not affected.
  • TensorFlow prints CUDA or XLA log lines on computers without an NVIDIA GPU, for example failed call to cuInit. You can ignore them.
  • uv prints warning: The --torch-backend option is experimental when it installs PyTorch for a GPU.
  • With PyTorch, each worker prints a FutureWarning that torch.jit.load is deprecated.
  • The ROCm build of PyTorch (AMD GPUs) prints (null): No such file or directory, in your system’s language, when it starts.
